purpose: Product discovery and design exploration only

prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create an exceptionally art-directed, beautiful actual desktop scanner application interface, 1536x1024 landscape. This is a fresh design exploration for Open Scanline. The previous generic wizard with teal buttons and wide forms was rejected by the user as generic and ugly. DO NOT use a wizard, sidebar, dashboard, rounded cards, huge stretched form inputs, teal, default bootstrap controls, or a marketing landing page. This must feel like a crafted professional creative tool with a clear runnable scan job.
DIRECTION A: "Paper edition". Editorial book-design typography meets quiet precise desktop software. Warm chalk #F3F0E8 canvas, near-black #262622 text, restrained persimmon #C24E2F action color, warm gray hairlines. Large elegant modern SERIF job title paired with beautifully spaced utilitarian sans labels and monospaced technical values. Flat surfaces, confident asymmetry, strong margins, square edges, no gradients, no floating shadows except extremely subtle physical paper layering. Sophisticated generous negative space. Realistic legible interface typography.
Full canvas is the app. Thin top masthead at x48 y36 "OPEN SCANLINE" in tracked small sans; tiny subtitle beside it "Local scanning"; at far right small text "New scan" and "Help". Beneath a hairline, upper-left small rust label "01 / PREPARE". Main title "September invoices" in elegant 54px serif, with a small pencil icon to suggest editable PDF basename. Under title compact sentence "Three sheets. Both sides. One searchable PDF."
Below, divide the workspace into a 60% left paper work area and 40% right job-control column using whitespace and one fine vertical line. Left work area has a restrained row of SIX overlapping offset cream paper outlines in three front/back pairs, showing only large page numbers 01–06 and faint neutral placeholder lines, NOT captured invoice content. Above these paper shapes small caption "OUTPUT PLAN · NOT A PREVIEW"; beneath them a thin horizontal rule with three paired marks labelled "Sheet 1", "Sheet 2", "Sheet 3", reinforcing duplex. Below the diagram put a serif subheading "One document, six image files." and two perfectly aligned plain output rows with small type labels "PDF" and "PAGES": "September-invoices.pdf" / "September-invoices-pages/". The paper visualization is the conceptual heart: tangible page assembly with plenty of breathing room, not decorative stacked cards.
Right job-control column around 400px wide, delicate section heading "CAPTURE". Compact inline underlined editable field rows rather than form boxes: "Scanner" value "Office scanner" chevron, small secondary "Network · eSCL · example device"; "Feed" "Document feeder" chevron; "Sides" select "Both sides" with small two-sided paper icon; "Limit" compact minus 6 plus and suffix "image sides"; small helper "3 double-sided sheets maximum"; "Resolution" "300 dpi" chevron. Delicate divider then "TEXT & IMAGE": toggle "Searchable PDF" on; "Tesseract · English" underline chevron, small label "Available in this example"; "Image corrections" "None" chevron; "Password" "Off" chevron. These controls are compact and elegant with clear interactive affordances.
Bottom across full width a very pale darker-cream band 120px tall with thin top rule. Left label "SAVE TO" and path "Documents / Scans" plus small underlined "Change". Secondary note "PNG pages save during capture; the PDF follows successful acquisition." Right a striking rectangular persimmon button with white text "Scan 3 sheets" and a slim right arrow. Beneath button tiny "Up to 6 image sides".
Do not display accounts, upload, cloud, history, presets, OCR scores, AI, thumbnails of supposedly captured documents, page reordering or resume. Scanner and Tesseract availability are illustrative. Output includes individual PNG files and PDF. All names fictional. Aim for the deliberate typographic quality of a premium publishing tool, with a rich visual hierarchy and coherent purposeful page metaphor. Actual controls need to be readable and usable.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a beautiful rigorously art-directed actual desktop scanner interface 1536x1024 landscape for Open Scanline, DIRECTION B "Scan instrument". The same real task is three double-sided paper sheets scanned as 6 logical sides at 300 dpi, saved as September-invoices.pdf with Tesseract English searchable text and individual PNG pages. This must be meaningfully different from a warm editorial paper workspace, not a palette swap. Think calibrated optical instrument combined with a premium audio workstation: quiet near-black navy matte canvas #171D26, precise ice-white sans typography, muted steel labels, acid-lime #D2F16A active indicator and main control, exceptionally disciplined alignment. Do NOT render fake hardware knobs, neon sci-fi, gradients, glows, beveled buttons or decorative machinery. No sidebar, wizard, cards, dashboard charts, branding hero or marketing prose.
The interface is organized around an acquisition-to-output routing strip, clear measurable limits and a bottom command shelf. All functional editable controls in 3 continuous horizontal zones across the full canvas, no boxed panels.
Top slim 70px masthead: "OPEN / SCANLINE" left in crisp white 22px sans, "LOCAL ACQUISITION" small mono at center, "B / SCAN INSTRUMENT" right subtle. Below 36px serif-free title "September invoices" left, small lime dot + "Ready to scan" right; small mono subtitle "September-invoices.pdf". Hairline divider.
Middle large routing area from y200 to y580: left station "01 / INPUT" with small high quality wireframe feeder glyph and label "Office scanner", subline "eSCL · illustrative device"; below inline chooser "Document feeder" with chevron. Center wide area "02 / ACQUISITION" with six tall narrow ruled lanes arranged as three pairs, each labelled "01 FRONT", "02 BACK", "03 FRONT", "04 BACK", "05 FRONT", "06 BACK". Each lane a blank dark paper outline with a small pending ring in center, explicitly captioned "PLANNED SIDES · NOT SCANNED". Delicate thin horizontal arrow links input to planned lanes to right station "03 / OUTPUT". Output station shows one strong white outlined document icon marked PDF, label "Searchable PDF", plus six small stacked lines "6 PNG files". Tiny readable note "Built after capture succeeds". No real page previews, confidence values or measured statistics.
Below diagram full-width control rail y610–760 separated by horizontal hairlines. Six clear compact labelled control groups with white underlined values and visible dropdown chevrons: "SIDES" "Both sides"; "LIMIT" "− 6 +" with small "3 sheets maximum"; "RESOLUTION" "300 dpi"; "TEXT" "Tesseract / English" with small lime check "Available in this example"; "CORRECTIONS" "None"; "PASSWORD" "Off". Controls are actual readable UI with at least 18px type. No pretend physical switches.
Bottom y800–1000 execution shelf, same dark surface. Left "DESTINATION" muted uppercase 12px, next line folder glyph and "Documents / Scans" with underlined "Change". Smaller two lines "September-invoices.pdf" and "September-invoices-pages / page_001.png …". Right large acid lime rectangular button with dark navy text "Start acquisition" and crisp play triangle, small footer "Up to 6 sides · Stop available during capture".
Very bottom small calm note "Completed page files remain if the job stops before PDF assembly." All text rendered legibly; strong negative space, visually sophisticated. No web app generic field boxes. UI readiness and device support are sample scenario assumptions, no actual hardware is claimed. No pause/resume, queue, cloud, accounts, AI detection, reorder, scanning preview before capture.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Refine the attached NEWLY GENERATED dark Open Scanline design concept into a mature, understated, beautifully finished working desktop utility. User liked the direction but asks for less generic AI aesthetic. Use reference for dark palette and precise working-tool attitude only. Redesign composition substantially. Generate one high fidelity flat app screenshot 1536x1024. No marketing, no giant decorative scanner illustration, no giant paper outline illustrations, no six repeated placeholder cards, no diagram arrows, no all-caps tracked section labels, no gradients or neon lime glow, no monospaced text everywhere. Deliberate quiet craft. Very dark warm slate #1d2329, slightly lighter #252c32 work surface, warm off-white #e7e9e4, muted silver labels, desaturated pale sage #c1d6a4 primary button. Use one exceptionally legible humanist sans family (like Inter) with tabular numerals. 18-22px body at this image size. Thin understated borders, 4px corner radii only on interactive controls. Refined desktop proportions, generous but useful whitespace.
Window chrome: slim row "Open Scanline" left and subtle native minimize/maximize/close controls right. Next row at y110 small "New scan" left, text action "Use an image file" right. Main editable job title "September invoices" 38px medium-weight sans at x64 y175, with quiet pencil icon. Below title plain secondary "Save a searchable PDF and individual page images."
Main workspace y265 to750: two columns with a fine vertical separator x680. LEFT x64 to620 is compact settings with title "Scanner". A carefully drawn 56px high selection control "Office scanner" with subline "eSCL · example device" and chevron; then inline label/value rows with subtle underlines: "Paper source" "Document feeder" chevron; "Sides" segmented choice "One" and selected "Both"; "Resolution" "300 dpi" chevron. Below title "Page limit"; compact number stepper "−  6  +" next to text "sides", clear helper "3 double-sided sheets maximum." Under helper one compact horizontal diagram only 48px tall: three bracketed numbered pairs [1 2] [3 4] [5 6] as simple fine ruled ticks, not cards or images. Caption "Planned order" and "Device order is preserved". This conveys physical sides without decorative fill.
RIGHT x744 to1470: title "Files"; two functional output rows, each with small 20px line file icon: label "PDF" above editable underline "September-invoices.pdf"; label "PNG pages" above editable underline "September-invoices-pages/". Under rows a separator. "Searchable text" with sage toggle on and next row "Tesseract · English" dropdown; tiny secondary "Available in this example". Final two compact disclosure rows "Image corrections" value "None" and "PDF password" value "Off". Use sensible 20px typography and 36px row rhythm.
Bottom shelf y820 to1024 separated by rule; left label "Save in" above compact path "Documents / Scans" with "Choose folder" underlined text. Below subtle text "Page images save first. The PDF is created after scanning succeeds." Right sage button about 240x58 labelled "Start scan", small below "Up to 6 sides". Above primary button optional tiny neutral status "Ready". NOT READY TO SCAN giant badge.
Composition should feel like precise, humane desktop software designed by an experienced designer, not a terminal, diagram, slide or template. No avatar, cloud, dashboard metrics, queue, OCR scores, upload, auto naming rules, page reorder, resume. Show ONLY the specified features. File names are fictional. Keep every control credible, text sharp and layout uncluttered. Dark instrument design but restrained and pleasant, with no unused huge graphic areas.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Use the attached newly generated Open Scanline refined dark interface as the exact visual and spatial reference. Produce the next state in its task, landscape 1536x1024. Keep the same window chrome, dark slate, restrained pale sage, readable humanist sans type, title "September invoices", left and right columns and fixed bottom destination shelf. This is a real usable proposal, not a dramatic redesign, slide, marketing graphic or dashboard. No gradient or glow.
Window header Open Scanline. Replace small "New scan" above title with "Scanning". Keep the title size and position. Under title "4 of 6 image sides saved".
LEFT column replace editable scanner settings with compact progress. Heading "Scanning"; large but restrained numeral "4 / 6" 44px and adjacent "sides saved"; a thin sage horizontal progress bar at two thirds, label "Capture progress", no total-job percent or time estimate. Under it the same three paired side markers [1 2] [3 4] [5 6], first four filled sage with small check shapes, last two outlined, legend "Saved" and "Waiting". Plain status below "Waiting for the next side". Thin divider then compact read-only rows "Office scanner" / "Document feeder · Both sides" / "300 dpi · Limit 6 sides". Below small info "Text recognition runs between captured sides." No paper preview, fake OCR text or scores.
RIGHT column keep heading "Files". Same PDF row icon and filename "September-invoices.pdf", small status "Not created yet". Below PNG folder row "September-invoices-pages/" with "4 files saved". Under that a quiet compact list without boxes or cards: page_001.png Saved, page_002.png Saved, page_003.png Saved, page_004.png Saved, status words right aligned with check marks. A simple subtle divider then "PDF assembly follows capture and text recognition." No ability to edit destination or settings while working.
BOTTOM shelf preserve "Save in" and "Documents / Scans", no Choose folder action during scan. Helper "Cancelling keeps completed page files. The PDF may not be created." Right outlined modest button "Cancel scan". No back, new scan, pause, resume, retries, or continue button during the operation. The use-image-file action from the setup screen is absent while capture is running. No invented job capabilities. Same understated craftsmanship and precise spacing as reference.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Generate completion state of the attached newly generated refined Open Scanline desktop design. Use it as exact layout, color, typography reference, landscape 1536x1024. Calm plain dark utility, slate, off-white, muted sage. No giant check illustration, confetti, congratulatory copy, hero, marketing, glowing color or new layout. Match same app header, title position, two working columns, fixed destination shelf. Header "Open Scanline"; small context "Saved"; title "September invoices"; subline "6 sides saved as a searchable PDF and PNG images."
LEFT column title "Scan complete". Then compact result rows around 24px line text "6 image sides" / "3 double-sided sheets" / "300 dpi". Same small paired numbered marker line [1 2] [3 4] [5 6], all six with sage check marks. Fine divider. A plain neutral stop explanation "Stopped at the 6-side limit." and helper "Check the feeder for any remaining sheets." Below source details "Office scanner" / "Document feeder · Both sides". Below small line "Text recognition: Tesseract · English" and subdued helper "Recognized text can contain errors." No OCR score or invented recognition data.
RIGHT column title "Files". Keep the same file locations and positions: PDF file icon 20px, "PDF" label, "September-invoices.pdf" with small check + "Saved · 6 pages"; next "PNG pages", "September-invoices-pages/" and "Saved · 6 files". Then compact six rows page_001.png Saved, page_002.png Saved, page_003.png Saved, page_004.png Saved, page_005.png Saved, page_006.png Saved. Fine rules only. No cards, file preview, embedded document content, edit buttons, Open file, copy button, cloud share or folder opening controls.
BOTTOM shelf "Saved in" then "Documents / Scans", subline "The PDF and page images are stored on this computer." Right two understated buttons "New scan" outlined and "Done" muted sage, about 160px each. No cancel or start acquisition now. This is the terminal state only after the PDF and every page output have been successfully published. Fictional sample job. Preserve the readable quiet exact design of the reference.
